function: Learns per-time-slot beam illumination (which cell each beam serves) for two neighboring LEO satellites with full frequency reuse to maximize throughput, without ground control (pp. 1, 3).
system: 2 LEO satellites (780 km), Ka-band 20 GHz, 500 MHz; phased arrays, 10 beams and 37 cells each, 10 cells overlap, full frequency reuse; no RIS (pp. 1, 4).
method: Multi-agent DRL, actor-critic with centralized critic and one actor per beam, plus policy-approximation networks inferring other agents; centralized offline training, distributed onboard inference (pp. 1, 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated: free-space path loss, Rician fading with elevation-dependent parameters from [12], 3GPP TR 38.811 multi-beam antenna pattern, Poisson packet arrivals per cell; no dataset (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training converges near iteration 500 (3600 steps each, Fig. 2); evaluation sweeps demand 400-2400 Mbps and queue length 2-7; no separate training and test conditions stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: Random, NSBC-Greedy [15], DBSO [6]. Learned: NCS-DRL [16], single-satellite DRL beam hopping, non-cooperative (p. 4).
metrics: Normalized reward, system throughput (Mbps), and probability of cell illumination; throughput vs demand and cache queue length (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Online operation count: sum of W_{l-1}*W_l*delta^2 over layers for actor and policy networks, times K_tot beams (Eqs. 15-18); no numeric value (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "this paper adopts the Rician fading model to characterize the communication channel". Not met: Rician fading with parameters from [12], free-space path loss and Poisson traffic are custom; 3GPP TR 38.811 is cited only for the multi-beam antenna pattern; no standard channel, dataset, or measurement.
q2_support: p. 5: "under increasing communication demand". Not met: throughput is swept over demand and cache queue length (Figs. 3 and 4); the paper never states that a model trained under one setting is tested under another.
q3_support: p. 4: "NCS-DRL Algorithm [16]: Single satellite beam hopping based on deep reinforcement learning". Non-learned Random, NSBC-Greedy [15] and DBSO [6] are listed on the same page; all five methods are compared on throughput (Fig. 3a, p. 5).
q4_support: p. 5: "the total online computational complexity of the". Eqs. (15)-(18) give the operation count as a sum over layers of W_{l-1}*W_l*delta^2 for the actor and policy networks, times the number of beams.
q5_support: p. 4: "The key link parameters are summarized in Table I, partially adapted from [4]". Not met: custom Python simulation with parameters in Table I; no link to code or data and no public dataset.
notes: Area 6: learned control of beams in satellite links (beam illumination per cell and slot), so it passes the above-PHY check by the satellite exception, although the paper also models cell queues and traffic. Reviewer checks. (1) q1 is 0: 3GPP TR 38.811 is cited only for the multi-beam antenna pattern (p. 2), while fading (Rician, [12]), path loss and traffic are custom; if the reviewer counts the antenna pattern as a TR 38.811 model, q1 becomes 1. (2) q3 counts NCS-DRL [16], a published DRL beam-hopping scheme, as the learned baseline; the paper attributes the gap to the policy approximation network (p. 4), so it could be read as an ablation. (3) q4 rests on the operation-count formulas of Section IV-C (p. 5), no numeric value.
